brief: Goldman's flow-of-funds note argues the technical setup for US equities is improving even as sentiment and the macro backdrop stay unresolved. Multiple flow and positioning signals point the same way: November is seasonally the second-biggest month for corporate buybacks, with blackout exits rising from about 10% by week's end to 48% by month's end; the Sentiment Indicator at -1.3 sits in a band that has corresponded to a +2% average one-month forward return; October mutual fund year-end selling, a major supply source, is nearing its end; foreign investors, still quiet since 2009, have historically bought equities for six months after midterm elections; global equity funds saw $12bn of net inflows in the week of October 7, and money market funds took in $166.37bn the same week, cash Goldman says is ready to deploy into year-end. Separately, hedge funds rotated out of crowded Info Tech longs and into Industrials last week, while CTAs remain under-positioned and short Russell stocks. A Bloomberg study cited by Goldman finds narrow-breadth episodes since 1995 were followed by above-median S&P gains, challenging the doomsday narrative around market concentration.
